# FFmpeg i686 for the x86 build (32-bit Windows 7)

**Precompiled** package of shared FFmpeg 9.0.2 (DLLs) for the
**x86 Windows** build (32-bit Win7). It is the engine of the `FfmpegBackend` when
`NEVERTUBE_X86_FFMPEG_BUILD` is active (see `CMakeLists.txt`).

## Why it is vendored

**There is no public FFmpeg build for 32-bit Windows.** The two
maintained sources are x64 only, and MSYS2 retired the i686 target:

- `gyan.dev` — "All builds are 64-bit" (and since 2026 it requires Windows 10+).
- `BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds` — `win64`-only assets.
- MSYS2 — `mingw-w64-i686-ffmpeg` no longer exists.

Since there is no binary to download, it is cross-compiled once with
`tools/build_ffmpeg_i686.sh` and vendored here. The CI neither downloads nor
compiles FFmpeg: it uses this package directly.

## Properties (verified)

- **i686** (PE32, Windows 7+): compiled with `-D_WIN32_WINNT=0x0601`.
- **LGPL v2.1+** (`--disable-gpl --disable-nonfree`): redistributable with the
  proprietary app by linking it dynamically. See `LICENSE.LGPLv2.1`.
- **TLS via schannel** (`--enable-schannel`): FFmpeg does not need OpenSSL
  DLLs; it uses the system's `Secur32.dll`/`ncrypt.dll`/`CRYPT32.dll`. (The app
  still uses OpenSSL 1.1 only for Qt's HTTPS.)
- **DXVA2 for H.264** (`--enable-dxva2 --enable-hwaccel=h264_dxva2`): the
  machine's hardware acceleration (backend Phase 4).
- **No external dependencies**: `--enable-w32threads` avoids
  `libwinpthread-1.dll`; the llvm-mingw runtime is static (there is no
  `libgcc_s_*.dll` or `libunwind.dll`). The DLLs only import system DLLs
  present in Win7 SP1 (`msvcrt`, `KERNEL32`, `USER32`, `ole32`, `WS2_32`,
  `Secur32`, `ncrypt`, `CRYPT32`, `bcrypt`).
- **Win7-clean imports**: no DLL imports W8+ symbols
  (`GetSystemTimePreciseAsFileTime`, `*ForDpi`, `GetDpiForMonitor`,
  `api-ms-win-*`, `WaitOnAddress`, `RoGetActivationFactory`, …). It is verified
  by `tools/build_ffmpeg_i686.sh` with `objdump -p` (the same gate as the CI).
  The gate covers the `ffmpeg.exe` too: it also runs on the Win7 machine.

## Contents

```
include/   public headers (libavcodec, libavformat, libavutil, libswscale, libswresample, libavfilter)
lib/       MSVC import-libs (avcodec.lib, avformat.lib, avutil.lib, swscale.lib, swresample.lib)
bin/       runtime DLLs (avcodec-63.dll, avformat-63.dll, avutil-61.dll, swscale-10.dll, swresample-7.dll,
           avfilter-12.dll, libmp3lame-0.dll) AND the CLI (ffmpeg.exe)
LICENSE.LGPLv2.1        (FFmpeg)
LICENSE.LGPLv2-LAME.txt  (LAME, the mp3 encoder)
```

`CMakeLists.txt` uses `include/` + `lib/`; the workflow copies `bin/*.dll` into
the installer. The `.lib` files are generated by FFmpeg itself (`dlltool -m i386`)
and are linkable by MSVC.

### The CLI (`ffmpeg.exe`)

The app does NOT need it to play (it links the DLLs above), but the
**downloader** does: it runs the ffmpeg to join the two tracks of a
downloaded video (`-c copy` into an MKV). Without it the download finishes
but the mux fails ("ffmpeg was not found").

It is **our own build**, not a downloaded binary: the same cross-compile,
with the muxers and the CLI enabled. It is 405 KB and it uses the DLLs that
are already next to it (there is nothing extra to install).

The mp3 encoder IS there: **LAME is LGPL v2, not GPL** (FFmpeg's own list
of the GPL libraries does not carry `libmp3lame`), so the LGPL build links it
and the "solo el audio" download is an mp3. The recipe compiles LAME as a
DLL (`libmp3lame-0.dll`) and FFmpeg links it against it.

## Exact configuration

FFmpeg 9.0.2, llvm-mingw 20260922 (variant **msvcrt**), nasm 2.16.03.
Trimmed to what the app uses:

- decoders: h264, vp9, av1, aac, opus, mp3, vorbis, flac, pcm_s16le, pcm_f32le
- demuxers: hls, mov, matroska, mpegts, aac, mp3, ogg, flv, concat
- protocols: file, http, https, tcp, tls, crypto, data, cache, httpproxy, concat, pipe
- parsers: h264, aac, av1, opus, mpegaudio, vorbis
- bsfs: h264_mp4toannexb, aac_adtstoasc, extract_extradata, vp9_superframe(_split), av1_frame_merge/split
- muxers: matroska, mp4, mp3, ipod (the downloader joins the tracks with them)
- encoders: aac, libmp3lame (the mp3 of the "solo el audio"; LAME is LGPL v2
  and it is compiled by the recipe as libmp3lame-0.dll)
- filters: the eleven that the CLI needs (aformat, anull, atrim, crop, format, hflip, null, rotate, transpose, trim, vflip): the CLI of FFmpeg requires avfilter
- no avdevice (the CLI does not open devices)

Result: ~9 MB of DLLs (versus ~15 MB with the full FFmpeg set and the
64.7 MB of `libmpv-2.dll`).

## Verification performed

- Demux + real decoding under Wine of the repo clips
  (`h264.mp4`, `vp9.webm`, `av1.mkv`) and of an h264+aac fMP4 HLS generated with
  the system ffmpeg (`-count_frames`: 75 video + 142 audio).
- Real TLS handshake under Wine against an `https://` (`[tls] Handshake …`),
  confirming the schannel path.
- Win7 imports gate with `objdump -p` over the 5 DLLs: clean.

## Rebuild

```sh
tools/build_ffmpeg_i686.sh            # writes to third_party/ffmpeg-win32
```

The script downloads llvm-mingw, nasm and the FFmpeg source, compiles and writes
out the same layout. It is the source of truth for the provenance of this package.
